key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification improves WC-12Co coating surface finish and scratch performance, with 30 N emerging as the best overall static contact load in this study.
engineering_relevance: For detonation-sprayed hard coatings, tuning UNSM load can meaningfully trade roughness reduction against adhesion/cohesion behavior, helping identify a practical processing window.
method: Detonation-sprayed WC-12Co coatings were treated by UNSM at 10, 20, 30, and 40 N static contact load.
Surface and cross-sectional changes were measured using profilometry and SEM.
Mechanical response was evaluated by instrumental indentation and progressive-load scratch testing.
evidence_signal: Ra decreased from 1.468 ± 0.098 μm at 10 N to 1.158 ± 0.244 μm at 40 N, while 30 N gave the lowest residual scratch depth (5.5 ± 1.8 μm) and the highest cohesive critical load (Lc1 = 50.2 N).
watch_item: The conclusion is provisional because coating thickness varied strongly across samples, and the scratch indenter could extend beyond the coating boundary on the thinnest specimens.
paper_title: The Effect of Ultrasonic Surface Modification of Nanocrystals on the Surface, Microstructure, and Mechanical Properties of a WC-12Co Coating Deposited by Detonation Spraying
